source.title: From Geometric Recovery to Causal Validation: A Reproducible Audit of Sparse Autoencoder Features, from Superposition Geometry to Causal Inertness

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a from-scratch, multi-seed reproduction of the superposition phase diagram, measuring feature sharing across sparsity and overcompleteness settings.
record.gate_note: The paper's background statement about polysemantic neurons and results it attributes to cited studies are not counted as this study's findings. Its main phase-diagram experiment measures feature directions in a synthetic bottleneck model, not neuron-level semantic responses. The production-SAE collision and causal-inertness results are recorded as related findings, but do not directly measure neuron polysemanticity or the language-model neuron claim.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces the Elhage et al. superposition phase diagram from scratch, with 3 seeds per cell. It shows sparse features packed into fewer dimensions as sparsity and overcompleteness rise, and none in a capacity-sufficient control. That is evidence for V3's mechanism: more sparse features than dimensions, packed together. The hidden layer is a linear bottleneck, h = Wx, with no privileged neuron basis, so it measures feature directions, not individual neurons. The originals (Zoom In, SoLU) are not this method, so this is T2, not T1. The SAE and GPT-2 audits concern SAE atoms, not neurons.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but incomplete. The authors conclude three things. Sparse features pack non-orthogonally when sparsity makes it cheap, with an under-training artifact and a diffuse-sharing regime. TopK beats L1 because of L1 shrinkage. Geometric recovery is not causal: up to 77% of matched features are inert in a degraded SAE and 9% in a good one, split into structural (antipodal) and competitive inertness, and into read-inertness and write-inertness. The GPT-2 atom collisions are unresolved as to mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: The paper describes a from-scratch, multi-seed reproduction of Elhage et al.'s superposition phase diagram using synthetic sparse inputs and an importance-weighted reconstruction model. The paper also studies SAE recovery and causal interventions beyond the phase-diagram measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: Superposition outcomes vary with feature-to-hidden-dimension ratio and input sparsity. At high sparsity, the step budget matters: the initial 1,500-step run produced apparent superposition in the ratio-1 control, resolved by 8,000 steps.

fits_no_version.finding: In toy TopK SAEs, some decoder atoms match a feature at cosine up to 0.9998 yet never fire on 500 feature-present samples: 2/22 in the good SAE, 3/22 in the bad one. The cause is antipodal pairs sharing one atom under a positive-pass encoder.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder-geometry recovery of a superposed feature does not imply the SAE encoder activates for it; antipodal superposition produces structurally inert matches.

fits_no_version.finding: In gpt2-small-res-jb layer 8, a few SAE atoms are nearest matches for many semantically disjoint concept probe directions (atom 14149 for 8 of 83). This recurs across batches; the mechanism is unresolved.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A small set of production SAE atoms recur as nearest matches for unrelated concept probes; this may reflect dictionary under-splitting, probe artifacts, or polysemantic SAE features.

record.problems: The phase diagram uses a small synthetic model and 3 seeds per cell; its results do not directly establish neuron-level semantic behavior in production models. The deterministic causal audit uses one seed per SAE and small recovered sets (22 features); the paper says its bootstrap intervals quantify within-sample, not across-seed, uncertainty. The real-model census covers one SAE hook layer, 83 concepts, and only 7 matches above its lowered cosine threshold; the probe direction is a proxy for unavailable ground truth, and the authors do not resolve whether atom collisions are genuine polysemantic hubs or artifacts.
record.rows_left_out: The initial and deterministic SAE audits report additional ablation and steering specificity summaries, but these measure causal efficacy of SAE feature matches rather than any tested claim version; only the deterministic inertness census relevant to the unrepresented SAE-feature claim is retained. L1-versus-TopK recovery and activation-refinement results concern SAE training and shrinkage, not neuron polysemanticity or the tested superposition-geometry outcomes.

untested.parts: Whether individual neurons, i.e. a privileged basis with a nonlinearity, become polysemantic through this packing. The toy bottleneck is linear and the measure is feature-direction geometry, not neuron responses. Trained vision or language models are not tested.
No transformer MLP neurons measured; the GPT-2 audit is on residual-stream SAE atoms.
Not tested on neurons. The ratio-1 control shows no superposition once fully trained, but apparent superposition under under-training; neither is a neuron-level measure.
No activation-function or architecture comparison of neuron polysemanticity; L1 vs TopK concerns SAE recovery.
Not tested; the GPT-2 atom collisions are explicitly unresolved.
Not tested on neurons. The Di blind spot and training-budget artifact show feature-superposition classification is measurement-dependent, but not for neuron polysemanticity.

missing.what: Decayed-importance 32→8 model at s=0.95 fully drops the 10 lowest-importance features and represents 22 in 8 dims. This is more features than dimensions packed under sparsity, bearing on V3.
Mean Di over the full sparsity × ratio grid and pooled Di distributions at 8× (single peak at 1 at s=0; spread at 0.6-0.9; cluster at 0.08 at s=0.99)

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's caption says more overcompleteness needs less sparsity, but the data show the reverse: ratio 2 transitions by s=0.3, ratios 4 and 8 near s=0.6. The text itself says 4× and 8× transition later. The low-sparsity '1.00 dedicated' cells at ratios ≥2 cannot be genuine, given the paper's own point that Di misses dropped features. Those rows are set to cannot_determine, which is why the reader's limits_scope label for r8, r9, r15, r16 is dropped. The study's main contribution is about SAE evaluation, not neuron polysemanticity.

versions.untested_parts: No vision model or image input is studied; the toy inputs are synthetic.
No MLP neurons in transformer language models are measured for responses to tokens or contexts.

The paper tests superposition geometry in a synthetic model and connects antipodal pairs to SAE matches. It does not measure whether individual trained-network neurons are polysemantic, nor establish that this mechanism explains neuron-level polysemanticity in production models.
It does not test polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
The L1-versus-TopK comparison concerns SAE recovery, not the share of polysemantic neurons across activations or architectures. No modern-convnet or neuron-polysemanticity comparison is made.

The paper reports collisions between decoder atoms and unrelated concept probe directions, but explicitly does not resolve whether these are genuine shared features, proxy-direction artifacts, or polysemantic hub features. It does not establish that canonical polysemantic neurons detect one coherent feature.
It compares geometric matching with causal interventions on SAE features, but does not test how neuron-polysemanticity counts change with activation range or explanation-scoring choices.

relation.reason: Its own multi-seed results bear on whether features are packed under sparsity and overcompleteness.

tranche.reason: In the pack, Toy Models (arXiv:2209.10652) is a tested study with its own verdicts, so it is not the version's original. This study rebuilds Elhage's toy model and Di measure: a different method from the original's, aimed at the same question.

source_check.notes: The model is Elhage et al.'s ReLU-output toy model (linear 20-dim hidden layer, no privileged basis). All rows measure feature-direction geometry (Di, ||Wi||), not neuron responses. r26-r30 are ground-truth cosines in the 32→8 decayed model; r26/r29 and r27/r28 are duplicate pairs. The ratio-8, s=0.99 zero-dedicated cell is diffuse sharing (norm ≈ 1.40), not dropped features.

statements.correction: 2607.12166: x̂ = ReLU(WᵀWx + b), so a linear 20-dim hidden layer (no privileged basis) with a ReLU output. This is the same model type as the ReLU-output toy models in lw:kbwH and 2510.23671. Phase diagram uses uniform importance and 3 seeds per cell; the measure is Di plus a norm check.
statements.problem: Every Table 1 and r22 number is right. The conditions line calls 2607.12166 'a linear bottleneck' and sets it against 'ReLU-output models'. In fact its model is Elhage et al.'s ReLU-output model (Eq. 1).

statements.correction: Label for V3: none (method sensitivity only). Ratio 1 (20 features, 20 dims) at s=0.95/0.99 read about 8%/82% superposed at the 1,500-step default. At 8,000 steps: 1.00 ± 0.00 dedicated, loss ≈ 0. The authors call it under-training masquerading as superposition.
statements.problem: The numbers and the authors' attribution are right. 'Linear toy bottleneck' is accurate for the hidden layer. The limits_scope label is the error. The 1,500-step packing was an under-training artifact in a capacity-sufficient control cell, where V3 predicts no packing, and the authors resolved it. It is a method caveat, already recorded in V3.method_sensitivity[0].

statements.correction: Covers V3 support, V3 conflicts and V3 method sensitivity (training budget); not V3 against.
statements.problem: All numbers and the setup description are right: 'linear bottleneck' is accurate for the hidden layer, and 'settles' is fair as an existence proof by an independent author. But 'covers: V3 against' rests on the l1 limits_scope verdict, which should be none.
